 frameglide
 From a 30 fps console stream to 60–120 fps on your PC. 

frameglide streams your console to your Windows PC and draws new frames between the ones the game sends, live — a 30 fps game plays at 60, 90 or up to 120 fps to match your screen, sharpened to fit it. Nothing gets installed on the console, and the tool is free and open source.

[download-url]: 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 In one picture: your console sends 30 frames a second, real frames A, B, C, D; AI frames are drawn between each pair on your graphics card, the 1080p picture is scaled to your monitor — and your screen shows 60, 90 or up to 120 frames a second.

 🎯 Why
Consoles still lock many big titles to a 30 fps Quality mode, and a big, fast monitor makes every step of that slideshow painfully visible. Buying a mid-generation console refresh or a 120 Hz HDMI chain is a lot of money for one number. frameglide takes the stream your PC already receives and lets your graphics card do the rest: it generates the in-between frames with an open-source AI model in real time, scales the picture to your display, and gives you smooth motion from hardware you already own — for free, with no account and no tracking.

 ⚖️ Without / With
 Without frameglide With frameglide 
 --- --- 
 30 fps Quality mode looks choppy on a 90–120 Hz screen The same game plays at 60, 90 or up to 120 fps to match your display 
 The 1080p stream looks soft on a big monitor The picture is sharpened and scaled by AMD FSR 1 or NVIDIA RTX VSR 
 Big titles only: fast motion, replays and cutscenes stutter Instant replay saves the last 30 seconds to 5 minutes at the frame rate you see 
 A flat, untouched picture Live "looks": 14 built-in grades like Golden hour or Noir, or your own 
 Fiddly manual setup of streamers and AI runtimes One installer checks your PC, fixes what's off and tunes itself to your card 

 🚀 Quick Start
1. Get the installer: click Download at the top of this page and save FrameGlide-Setup.exe from the Releases page to your Downloads folder.
2. Check the installer before running it (optional): compare its SHA-256 hash with the one listed on the Releases page.
 powershell Get-FileHash "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\FrameGlide-Setup.exe" 
3. Run setup: double-click the file — Windows SmartScreen warns because the installer isn't code-signed yet, so click More info → Run anyway . Setup takes 10–20 minutes, never asks for admin rights, and downloads the AI runtime from official sources.
4. Connect your console once: for a PS5, follow Connect your PS5 in the app — turn on Remote Play on the console, sign in to PSN and register the console.
5. Press Play in the app, pick the game on your console, and play at your screen's refresh rate.

 ✨ Features
- Generate 1, 2 or 3 AI frames between every pair the console sends, about 9 ms each on an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, with the open-source RIFE model.
- Scale and sharpen the 1080p stream to your monitor with AMD FSR 1 in about 0.1 ms, or NVIDIA RTX Video Super Resolution.
- Stream from a PS5 over Remote Play on your home network through the open-source chiaki-ng — your controller connects to the PC.
- Capture any other source as an Experimental option: an Xbox through its app's window, or any console over HDMI through a capture card.
- Save instant replays as MP4 with the game's sound, plus a before & after video to compare frame generation off and on.
- Restyle the picture live with 14 built-in looks, save your own and share them as a short code.
- Keep 40–60 fps games even with the Experimental 40–60 fps smoother, and test your setup with the built-in 60 fps test mode.

 ⚙️ How it works
The console and your PC talk over your home network, the way the console maker's own Remote Play app does: chiaki-ng receives the stream, plays the sound and sends your button presses back, and a small patch to it — the frame tap — hands every video frame to frameglide. On your graphics card, the video decoder unpacks each frame and skips repeats, the AI cores draw the in-between frames with RIFE through TensorRT, the shader cores scale the result with FSR 1, and the display output shows a frame every refresh. With an Xbox app window or a capture card (Experimental), the frames come from the captured window or the card instead, and the rest is the same.

 🕹️ Usage
- PS5 over Remote Play (tested). Register the console once in the app, press Play , and a 30 fps Quality-mode game runs at 60, 90 or up to 120 fps on your monitor.
- Any console over HDMI (Experimental). Connect a capture card, pick Capture card on the Play page, and the same pipeline smooths and scales the picture.
- Instant replay. Press R in the video window to save the last 30 seconds to 5 minutes as an MP4 at the frame rate you see; B saves a before & after video ( Ctrl+Alt+R / Ctrl+Alt+B from any window).

 🛠️ Configuration
 Setting What it does Options 
 --- --- --- 
 Frame rate How many frames per second the screen gets 60 / 90 / up to 120, to match your display 
 Upscaler Scales the 1080p stream to your monitor AMD FSR 1 / NVIDIA RTX VSR 
 AI model Draws the in-between frames RIFE (default) / NVIDIA VFG for RTX 40–50 cards, optional download 
 Even out 40–60 fps Spaces frames of 40–60 fps games evenly over a 60 Hz stream On / off (on by default, Experimental) 
 Instant replay Length of the rolling recording Off / 30 s – 5 min 
 HDR Real colours from an HDR-capable PS5 stream Off / shown in SDR / HDR output (Experimental, off by default) 
 Looks Live color grade of the picture 14 built-in + your own, shared as a short code 

Change everything on the Settings page or press M in the video window; Auto-detect picks the best for your PC and explains each choice.

 ❓ Troubleshooting / FAQ
 Windows says "Windows protected your PC" — the installer isn't code-signed yet. Click More info → Run anyway ; setup installs only for your user and never asks for admin rights.
